claims.statement: build.sh is the host build entry point: it runs `trunk build --release` in `frontend/` and then `cargo build --release --features server`, and because it does not export SKIP_TRUNK, build.rs re-runs `trunk build --release` for the same assets during the cargo build.

desktop.sh builds the Tauri app with `cargo tauri build` in `desktop/` after exporting NO_STRIP=true, because linuxdeploy bundles a binutils too old to read the .relr.dyn sections modern distributions ship and fails the AppImage on the first library it strips; the same export and reason appear in dist.sh.

dist.sh produces the whole release matrix into dist/: it exports CROSS_CONTAINER_ENGINE=podman, prepends /opt/llvm-mingw/llvm-mingw-ucrt/bin to PATH and sets SKIP_TRUNK=true, then per target cross-builds `oxyromon --features server` plus the five format-crate CLIs (gdirs, nszrs, xdeltars, xpsrs, xsors) for four Linux targets (aarch64/x86_64 gnu+musl), x86_64-pc-windows-gnullvm and two apple-darwin targets, packing oxyromon and each CLI as a separate archive — .tar.xz for Linux/macOS, .7z for Windows — named with the target triple's vendor field trimmed (${target/-unknown/}, ${target/-pc/}), and running `cargo clean` between targets.

Cross-compilation keeps the web UI out of the containers: dist.sh exports SKIP_TRUNK=true and Cross.toml passes that variable through to the cross container under [build.env], while `(cd frontend && trunk build --release)` runs on the host at the top of each target iteration because the wasm bundle is target-independent.

The two macOS targets have no upstream cross images: Cross.toml maps aarch64-apple-darwin and x86_64-apple-darwin to ghcr.io/cross-rs/<target>-cross:local, so those images must be built locally before dist.sh can produce Apple artifacts.

Code signing applies only to Apple artifacts: for each darwin target dist.sh runs `rcodesign sign` on oxyromon and on each of the five format CLIs after cross build and before tarring, while Linux and Windows artifacts are shipped unsigned.

The Tauri desktop bundle is built for the host only and cannot be cross-compiled, because Tauri links the platform's own webview, which the cross images do not carry and for which no cross toolchain exists; Windows and macOS bundles require running the build on that operating system.

The desktop app ships no separate backend: tauri.conf.json declares externalBin binaries/oxyromon and runs desktop/scripts/stage-sidecar.sh as both beforeDevCommand and beforeBuildCommand; the script resolves the triple from TARGET_TRIPLE or `rustc -vV`, runs `cargo build --release --features server` from the repository root, and copies the binary to desktop/binaries/oxyromon-<triple>[.exe], a generated gitignored directory.

test.sh's second coverage pass is stale: it invokes `cargo llvm-cov --workspace --features oxyromon/nod,oxyromon/server,oxyromon/sevenz`, but the nod and sevenz features were removed in 0.25.0 when RVZ/WBFS and 7z/ZIP support became unconditional, so that invocation fails on unknown features and only the first pass (oxyromon/server) is valid.

docker.sh tags containers from the package version rather than from git: it reads .package.version out of Cargo.toml with tomlq and builds/pushes alucryd/oxyromon:<version>, :latest, <version>-alpine and :alpine from Dockerfile.archlinux and Dockerfile.alpine using sudo docker.

The automated Docker path is narrower than docker.sh: .github/workflows/docker.yml triggers on push to develop and builds and pushes only Dockerfile.archlinux with tags derived by docker/metadata-action from the git ref, so the version-pinned and Alpine tags exist only after someone runs docker.sh manually.

Both container images are self-contained build-and-run images that compile the web UI inside the image (neither sets SKIP_TRUNK): they install rustup, the wasm32-unknown-unknown target and trunk 0.21.14, run `cargo install --features server --root /usr --path .`, then remove the toolchain, caches and source tree. Alpine installs gcompat because trunk downloads prebuilt wasm-bindgen/wasm-opt binaries linked against glibc; Arch Linux disables pacman signature checking (SigLevel = Never) to keep the build scripted.

Both images pin runtime paths via environment (OXYROMON_DATA_DIRECTORY=/data, OXYROMON_ROM_DIRECTORY=/roms) with matching VOLUME declarations, but CMD is bare `oxyromon`; since main() only performs work inside `if let Some((subcommand, ...)) = matches.subcommand()`, a container started without an appended subcommand does nothing.

Format crates are published independently of oxyromon — own version, own CHANGELOG.md in oxyromon's format, `<crate>-<version>` git tags — which imposes a hard ordering rule: a crate must be published to crates.io before any oxyromon release that needs its new version, because the root declares each dependency with both `path` and `version` and the root's exclude list keeps `crates/` out of its own tarball.

oxyromon cannot be published while nod and sevenz-rust2 point at git, because crates.io rejects git dependencies: nod is pinned to tag v2.0.0-alpha.12 pending a crates.io release past 2.0.0-alpha.9, and sevenz-rust2 to fork revision d574d725e717d647c5ae67d3760e8af320920974 until upstream releases push_raw_block. Both are mandatory dependencies since 0.25.0 deleted the optional nod and sevenz features, so each pin must return to a version requirement before a release.

The published crate is deliberately smaller than the checkout: frontend/ and desktop/ are publish = false standalone crates with their own [workspace], and Cargo.toml excludes .github/, crates/, dist/ and tests/, so a crates.io install builds without the nested frontend package — the case build.rs guards by asserting frontend/ exists and by always creating target/assets for rust-embed.

AGENTS.md makes documentation part of every change rather than part of the release: each notable change must update the relevant README.md subcommand section to match real --help output and add a CHANGELOG.md entry under the current version's Features/Changes/Improvements/Fixes section, creating that version's block at the top of the file if absent, where 'current version' is the version field in Cargo.toml.

The release version is duplicated across four manifests that nothing checks against one another — Cargo.toml, frontend/Cargo.toml, desktop/Cargo.toml and desktop/tauri.conf.json (all 0.25.0) — while docker.sh derives its tags from the root value alone, so a bump must update all four by hand.

Because sqlx macros verify queries at compile time, changed queries require `cargo sqlx prepare -- --features server` to refresh the committed .sqlx/ offline data; a change left unprepared forces a live DATABASE_URL, which the cross containers and the Docker builds do not provide, so it breaks the release matrix rather than only a developer's machine.

No workflow builds or publishes release artifacts: continuous_integration.yml (push/PR to master) sets SKIP_TRUNK=true with TRUNK_VERSION pinned to 0.21.14, builds the web UI once, runs clippy twice — workspace with oxyromon/server, and --no-default-features --features use-rustls,mcp so mcp-only builds cannot rot — then `cargo build --release --features server` and workspace coverage, installing mame-tools and xdelta3 so reference-tool tests run instead of skipping.

Release archives do not bundle every codec oxyromon uses: `oxyromon info` still lists chdman and ctrtool as external dependencies next to the built-in crates, so a downloaded binary needs those tools on PATH for CHD and CIA work.

Shipping binaries are shaped by three divergent profiles: the root [profile.release] uses lto = "thin", codegen-units = 1, strip = true and panic = "abort" for oxyromon and the format CLIs, while frontend and desktop each declare their own size-oriented opt-level = "z" profiles because they are standalone crates outside the workspace.
